2608.23476.title: On the Threat Model of Weird Generalization and Emergent Misalignment
2608.23476.paper_summary: Narrow fine-tuning on small, domain-specific datasets can produce broad and surprising changes in model behavior-a phenomenon called weird generalization (WG). Yet, it remains unclear what features of the fine-tuning data are necessary for WG to arise. Here, we address this question by investigating a range of plausibly relevant features, including dataset size, composition, language, presentation style, and novelty relative to a model's parametric knowledge. Further, since WG evaluations rely on small question sets that assess the extent of the generalization, we also analyze how sensitive this measurement is to the set of questions used. Experiments with three open-weight models on four datasets show that the degree of WG (1) depends heavily on dataset composition and language (more than on size); (2) is greater for data familiar from pretraining than for novel data; and (3) is sensitive to the set of evaluation questions used. Collectively, these results indicate that WG is a product of quite fragile properties of both training and evaluation data. As such, we argue that WG is more plausible as an adversarial threat-requiring careful data engineering-rather than as a significant hazard inherent to routine fine-tuning.
2608.23476.paper_summary_zh: 狹義的微調在小型、特定領域的數據集上可以產生廣泛且令人驚訝的模型行為變化——這種現象被稱為奇怪的泛化（WG）。然而，目前尚不清楚微調數據的哪些特徵是WG出現所必需的。在這裡，我們通過調查一系列可能相關的特徵來解決這個問題，包括數據集大小、組成、語言、呈現風格，以及相對於模型參數知識的新穎性。此外，由於WG評估依賴於小型問題集來評估泛化的程度，我們還分析了這一測量對所使用問題集的敏感性。對三個開放權重模型在四個數據集上的實驗顯示，WG的程度（1）在很大程度上依賴於數據集的組成和語言（而不是大小）；（2）對於來自預訓練的熟悉數據，WG的程度大於對於新穎數據；以及（3）對所使用的評估問題集敏感。綜合這些結果表明，WG是訓練和評估數據的相當脆弱特性的產物。因此，我們認為WG更可能作為一種對抗威脅——需要謹慎的數據工程——而不是作為常規微調固有的重大危害。
